evidence.observation: A captain's log describes an Antares rendezvous. Ramart and Nellis introduce Charlie; Ramart reports a catastrophic prior crash and suggests onward transfer to relatives. Crew size and destination are speaker statements, not independently checked registries.

Kirk's log says Charlie was isolated for fourteen years. Charlie tells McCoy about wild food and functioning memory banks, and McCoy verbally reports a healthy examination. Neither the crash history nor biological condition is independently authenticated by this transcript.

Charlie offers Rand an unexplained gift, seeks her company and touches her without consent; Rand verbally distinguishes a welcome gift from unwanted conduct and asks him to consult officers. The text does not show the gift's physical origin.

Spock argues that survival required intelligent outside assistance and invokes unfavorable probe results; McCoy proposes edible vegetation and warns that probes can err. One line labeled MCCOY addresses 'Doctor' in a way that may signal a derivative speaker-label defect, not a newly established exchange.

A recreation-room performance and card exchange frame Charlie's pursuit of social approval. Charlie consults Kirk about Rand's objection; Kirk discusses appropriate restraint but is interrupted by a ship communication. Performance lyrics are not reproduced in these records.

Ramart attempts a warning but the transmission stops. Spock describes scanned debris as Antares remains; Charlie makes an ambiguous comment on construction. A galley officer reports unexpectedly transformed food. Cause is not established by the interrupted message or instrument report.

Spock suspects Charlie anticipated the Antares loss. Charlie plays chess and disputes the reported checkmate. Dialogue does not describe the board's visible movement or provide an authenticated camera-level account of any object alteration.

Rand introduces Tina and rejects Charlie's rudeness and possessive pursuit. Kirk explains that another person's feelings and refusal constrain Charlie's wishes. Charlie describes confusion and emotional distress; the record preserves both social instruction and his self-report without interpreting either as a diagnosis.

After a gym exchange, Kirk asks what happened to Sam and Charlie says he is gone; Charlie both denies intent and assigns blame. Uhura later reports phaser weapons absent. The text lacks an explicit stage direction showing Sam's fate or independent inventory evidence for weapons.

Officers conjecture powers resembling Thasian legends and debate containment. Asked directly about Antares, Charlie claims he removed a flawed component and offers both an inevitability rationale and an interpersonal grievance. The admission is evidence of his utterance, not an independently checked engineering reconstruction.

Kirk orders a course away from the colony while operators report navigation and communication interference. Charlie explicitly rejects the course change and says he can control Spock's speech. These statements do not by themselves authenticate every reported systems failure.

Rand explicitly tells Charlie to leave; he refuses. Shortly afterward, Kirk questions Rand's possible absence and Spock reports injured legs. Charlie refuses to specify Rand's fate. The source provides speech and reactions, not a resolved death or global identity event.

Kirk proposes saturating ship systems to strain Charlie's apparent control while confronting him. Officers later report restored navigation and a message attributed to Thasus. The mechanism and source of the reported communications remain subject to primary audiovisual and technical-context review.

A THASIAN-labeled voice says the group enabled Charlie's survival, returned affected people, and cannot safely leave him among humans. Kirk proposes training; Charlie strongly objects to leaving and fears isolation. Uhura later reports his departure aboard the other vessel. The collective's claims and any restoration are not independently verified by this derivative text.
